html:
A long drought in eastern Australia in the years around Federation, when the six colonies joined to form the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January 1901. It cut the country's sheep flock nearly in half.

Dry spells began in the mid 1890s, broken by some wetter years, and joined into a great drought that by 1902 covered more than half the continent. Rivers such as the Darling dried to chains of pools. Wheat crops failed and dust storms blew across Victoria and New South Wales. Sheep and cattle died in millions on overstocked runs, many of them already eaten bare by rabbits.

The drought came on top of the depression and bank crashes of the early 1890s. It showed that Australian farming had been built on the wet years and changed how farmers and governments thought about water, stocking rates and irrigation. Climate scientists now link such droughts to the El Niño cycle in the Pacific. See Australia and merino sheep.
